mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the 5-year moving average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-week simple moving average
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain positive despite trigger activation, or FEDFUNDS does not exceed the 5-week SMA in any of the observed windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in hourly wage growth (indirectly captured by HOUST) signals labor market weakness that precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% from the prior month while HOUST decreases by >2% from the prior month
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive 5-day windows following similar labor signals, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in retail sales ( proxy via INDPRO ) of at least 3 percentage points over two months predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investor sentiment deteriorates.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During a comparable two-month INDPRO decline episode, SPX 20-day forward returns were positive or not statistically different from the prior month's returns (t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a simultaneous rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates supply-side stress, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as market anticipates rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% while CPIAUCSL rises by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant SPX 20-day forward return in 10 analogous supply shock windows (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months without a corresponding rise in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 60-day forward returns as a soft landing is perceived.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 237 for the same months
failure_condition: Over 12 months in similar regimes, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline of zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in job openings ( proxy via RSAFS ) exceeding 200,000 for two consecutive months is associated with negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as market anticipates overheating and possible policy tightening.
failure_condition: During analogous labor expansion phases, SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time drop in consumer confidence ( proxy via HOUST ) of more than 15 points in a single month predicts negative S&P 500 20-day returns as risk aversion rises and equity valuations compress.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >15 points in a single month
failure_condition: In 5 analogous single-month confidence drops, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) without a corresponding decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests a supply-side imbalance that precedes S&P 500 positive 60-day forward returns as investors price in recovery.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥4% for four consecutive months and CPIAUCSL remains flat or rises over the same period
regime_hint: Prolonged supply contraction without inflationary response
failure_condition: No significant SPX 20-day forward return in 8 analogous supply contraction episodes (Granger causality p > 0.05).
